native_policy_decisions: Axum routing replaces Go ServeMux grammar, GODEBUG routing profiles and Go URL alias mechanics. Literal Agones routes and namespace/resource dispatch remain mapped.
HeaderMap/Uri/Method and serde own Rust request/response data. No source slice/map/nil/reflection behavior is reconstructed.
MIME quality/specificity ordering uses native parsing and stable sorting; served encodings and Agones JSON fallback remain explicit. Go ParseFloat and unstable-sort profiles are superseded.
Rustls resolves the most recently loaded certificate for each handshake, including clients without SNI; Go crypto/tls callback invocation/nil fallback mechanics are superseded.
Malformed admission input and invalid handler state use native HTTP/Result errors; no fabricated allowed request or nil-pointer runtime error.
Go response buffers, sniff tables, write-count overflow, status rendering, panic/recover and internal header/body profiles are not native HTTP completion requirements.

operations.agones_requirement: Serve configured HTTP/TLS ports with header/handshake timeouts, stop accepting on cancellation, preserve closed-server handling and retain connection drain in the parent scope.
Register literal discovery, resource and admission routes; retain dynamic route visibility, resource namespace/key dispatch and one shared mux owner.

Keep method/URI/host/header/body diagnostic fields and redact Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie and X-Api-Key. Rust ownership drops consumed request bodies.
Retain JSON, YAML and Kubernetes protobuf media types, JSON fallback, target metadata and resource snapshots. Native MIME parsing selects ordered acceptable alternatives.
Use Rustls validation/ALPN, keep the last successfully loaded certificate and share the native transport/router with the existing reload consumer.

Keep ordered operation/group/kind matching, response UID/defaults and handler-error Status construction. Missing input request returns 400; invalid handler-returned state becomes a normal server error rather than a reconstructed nil-pointer panic.

production_composition.ownership: One shared Axum route owner. The existing root task scope owns request and connection-drain futures; each native connection owns/join its Hyper protocol child scope. No detached application task or new application manager.
production_composition.shutdown: Listener shutdown retains drain in the existing parent scope. Root cancellation reaches request child tokens. Fatal listener errors abort connection tasks before cleanup; rejected drain ownership is awaited locally.
production_composition.streaming: A response head handshake plus a bounded two-frame channel feeds Axum Body. Closed receivers and cancelled requests produce native errors; frames are not claimed delivered to the network merely because they were queued.
